resolved_by: Supreme Court in Mathis v. United States, 579 U.S. 500 (2016), which held the modified categorical approach is unavailable when a statute lists multiple means to satisfy one element, rejecting the Eighth Circuit's approach
issue: Does the modified categorical approach apply when a statute lists alternative means rather than alternative elements, for purposes of determining whether a prior conviction qualifies as a predicate offense?
provision: Armed Career Criminal Act (18 U.S.C. § 924(e)); 28 U.S.C. § 2255(e) saving clause and § 2241

sides.position: Courts must apply the modified categorical approach whether a statute lists alternative elements or alternative means, with no means-elements distinction
cases: United States v. Mathis, 786 F.3d 1068, 1074–75 (8th Cir. 2015), rev'd, 579 U.S. 500 (2016)

quote: Before Mathis was decided, there was a circuit split over the “elements” versus “means” distinction in the context of predicate oﬀenses under the Armed Career Criminal Act.
cite: Michael Gamboa v. Charles Daniels, 26 F.4th 410 (7th Cir. 2022)
